title: Minimum Path Sum
description: Brute force to optimized: recursive exploration of both moves versus a 2D bottom-up DP grid.

blocks.text: Problem Summary: Given an m by n grid filled with non-negative numbers, find a path from the top-left to the bottom-right corner (moving only right or down) that minimizes the sum of numbers along the path.

blocks.caption: What goes in, what comes out

blocks.content: {"headers":["Aspect","Detail"],"rows":[["Input","grid of non-negative numbers"],["Output","The minimum sum along any valid path"],["Goal","dp[i][j] = grid value plus the cheaper of the cell above or the cell to the left"],["Constraints","Up to 200 by 200 grid"]]}

{"headers":["Signal in the problem","Pattern it points to"],"rows":[["\"Minimum sum path on a grid, moving only right or down\"","A direct variant of the Unique Paths grid DP: instead of SUMMING ways from the top and left neighbors, take the MINIMUM sum from them"]]}

blocks.text: Since only right or down moves are allowed, reaching any cell (i, j) must come from either directly above (i-1, j) or directly to the left (i, j-1). The minimum path sum to reach (i, j) is its own value plus whichever of those two neighbors offers the CHEAPER path sum so far.

blocks.title: Analogy: Finding the Cheapest Toll Route Through a City Grid, East or South Only
blocks.text: Picture a city grid where every intersection charges a toll, and travel is restricted to moving east or south. The cheapest way to reach any intersection is its own toll plus the cheaper of the two possible ways to arrive there, from the north or from the west.

blocks.caption: Cheapest path to a cell = its own value plus the cheaper of the cell above or the cell to the left

blocks.text: Minimum path sum = 7 (path 1 to 3 to 1 to 1 to 1, going right, right, down, down).

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: The top-left cell's minimum path sum is simply its own value, the starting point.

Observation 2: Every cell in the first row can only be reached by moving right repeatedly, so its cost is the running total along that row; similarly for the first column moving down.

Observation 3: For any other cell, since it can only be reached from above or from the left, its minimum path sum is its own value plus the SMALLER of those two neighbors' already-computed minimum path sums.
This leads to a 2D bottom-up DP grid, initializing the first row and column as running totals, and combining the minimum of the top and left neighbors for every other cell.
Recursively try both possible moves (right, down) from every cell, without memoization, exploring every possible path to the destination.
Why the code is written this way

items: Trying both moves recursively directly implements the definition.
This recomputes the same cells repeatedly across many different paths, costing exponential time; a 2D DP grid computes each cell exactly once.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(2 raised to (m+n)) without memoization.
Space: O(m+n) recursion depth.
Limitation: a 2D DP grid computes each cell's minimum path sum exactly once, reusing the top and left neighbors directly.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text: Build an m by n DP grid. Set dp[0][0] = grid[0][0]. Fill the first row as a running total (dp[0][j] = dp[0][j-1] + grid[0][j]), and the first column similarly (dp[i][0] = dp[i-1][0] + grid[i][0]). For every other cell, dp[i][j] = grid[i][j] + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]). Return dp[m-1][n-1].
Use a 2D bottom-up DP grid, initializing the first row and column as running totals, and taking the minimum of the top and left neighbors elsewhere.

Since movement is restricted to right or down, every cell's minimum path sum is fully determined by its top and left neighbors' already-computed minimum path sums (or a running total along the very first row or column, which have only one possible incoming direction); building the grid in row-major order guarantees both needed neighbors are always ready by the time each cell is processed.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(m times n).
Space: O(m times n), reducible to O(n) using a rolling row.

blocks.text: Minimum Path Sum is a direct variant of Unique Paths, swapping the "sum of ways" combination for a "minimum of costs" combination.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: If the interviewer says "minimum cost path on a grid, moving only right or down", think: 2D DP taking the minimum of the top and left neighbors.

items: How would you also reconstruct the actual path achieving the minimum sum, not just the sum itself?
Unique Paths and Dungeon Game, both closely related grid DP problems with a similar structure.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text: The unmemoized recursive approach costs O(2^(m+n)); the 2D DP grid costs O(m times n), the standard efficient solution.

items: Pattern: 2D bottom-up dynamic programming on a grid.
Core Idea: dp[i][j] = grid[i][j] + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]), since a cell can only be reached from above or from the left.
Time: O(2^(m+n)) for the brute force, O(m times n) for the DP approach.
Space: O(m+n) recursion depth for the brute force, O(m times n) (reducible to O(n)) for the DP approach.
Most Important Observation: the first row and column each have only one possible incoming direction, forming a running total.
Interview Difficulty: a foundational, easy to medium 2D DP problem.
One line memory trick: own value plus the cheaper of top or left.
